hero.h1: Power Rodding and Sewer Rodding in Mokena, IL
hero.sub: Water coming up through the basement floor drain, or every fixture in the house draining slowly at the same time, means the main line is blocked. We power rod it clear, show you what caused it and give you a flat price before we start. From our office on Jodi Road.

img.alt: J. Blanton plumber feeding the cable from a drum rodding machine into an outdoor sewer cleanout in a front yard

trust: 4.7 stars · 5,669+ Google reviews across all locations

blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

img.alt: Diagram showing a rodding cable fed through a cleanout access point into the main sewer line, with a cutting head clearing the blockage toward the street connection

blocks.h2: Signs Your Mokena Main Line Needs Rodding
blocks.intro: Call before it backs up all the way:

tiles.body: When the washer drains or someone showers, water rises at the lowest drain in the house.

tiles.h3: More Than One Fixture Is Slow
tiles.body: A slow toilet, tub and kitchen sink together point to the main line.
Air trapped behind a clog pushes back up through the bowls.
Roots grow back to the same joint, usually on about the same schedule.

blocks.h2: What Blocks Main Lines in Mokena
blocks.intro: Most Mokena homes were built in the last 35 years, so the clogs here are a little different from older towns.

items.h3: Wipes and Paper in a Low Spot
items.body: In a line with a slight sag, flushable wipes and paper settle and build up until the line stops.

items.h3: Fine Roots at a Loose Joint
items.body: Roots from yard trees planted with the subdivision find any gap and grow into a mat.
Years of cooking grease coat the line between the kitchen and the main.
If you need rodding every few months, [hydro jetting](/mokena/hydro-jetting) or a [sewer repair](/mokena/sewer-repair) is the better fix.

blocks.h2: Power Rodding Questions From Mokena Homeowners

items.q: What's the difference between power rodding and sewer rodding?
items.answer: They're the same thing. Power rodding just refers to the motorized machine that turns the cutting cable through your main line.

items.q: How often should my line be rodded?
items.preview: Only as often as roots or clogs come back.
items.answer: If roots have blocked the line before, once a year is common. If it was a one-time clog from wipes or grease, you may not need it again for years.

items.q: Can rodding damage a PVC sewer line?
items.preview: Not with the right cutting head.
items.answer: Not when it's done right. We match the cutting head to the pipe size and material, and the camera shows the condition of the line afterward.

items.q: Where is the cleanout in a Mokena home?
items.preview: Usually in the basement or just outside the foundation.
items.answer: In most homes built since the 1990s, there's a cleanout in the basement near where the main line leaves, and sometimes another one outside. We'll find it.

items.q: How much does power rodding cost in Mokena?
items.preview: It depends on access and the clog. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on where the cleanout is, how long the line is and what's blocking it. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
